description: Plaintiffs to file an amended complaint curing the shotgun defects
triggering_event: Entry of Doc. 35 fixing a date certain
governing_rule: Doc. 35 (Order of Magistrate Judge Howard), enforcing Fed. R. Civ. P. 8(a) and 10(b)
computation_method: No computation required. The order states a date certain: 'NO LATER THAN AUGUST 21, 2026.' Cross-check only: 2026-08-21 is a Friday, so no weekend or holiday roll would have applied had the date been computed.
consequence_of_missing: The Clerk was DIRECTED to submit the case to the magistrate judge at the expiration of the deadline. The order cautions that non-compliance 'may recommend to the District Judge that this case be dismissed.' Defendants have leave to move to dismiss if no amended complaint is filed.
verification_required: CONFIRM ON PACER/CM-ECF whether an amended complaint was filed on or before 2026-08-21, and if so at which docket number. As of 2026-09-21 the date has passed by 31 days and compliance is NOT established by any available source.
notes: The DATE is express and certain. date_status is needs-verification because COMPLIANCE is unknown, not because the date is doubtful. This is the highest-priority item in the matter.

description: Defendants to answer or otherwise respond to the amended complaint
governing_rule: Doc. 35 at 9 ('NO LATER THAN 14 DAYS after it is filed'), displacing the default period in Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(3)
computation_method: NOT COMPUTED. The triggering event - the filing of the amended complaint - is not established by any available source, so no date can be produced. Once the filing date is confirmed, the period is 14 days measured from FILING per the order's own words; the counting method under Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a) must then be applied to the confirmed date and checked against the court's calendar.
consequence_of_missing: Potential default or waiver of Rule 12 defenses as to the amended pleading. The period cannot run until the filing date is known.
ambiguity_description: The order measures the period from when the amended complaint 'is filed'. Fed. R. Civ. P. 15(a)(3) measures the default period from SERVICE of the amended pleading. Where a pro se plaintiff files and the defendants are served through CM/ECF, filing and service will usually coincide, but they need not. Which event controls should be treated as open until confirmed.
verification_required: Confirm the amended complaint's filing date AND its service date, and confirm whether the court intended filing or service as the trigger.
notes: Typed conditional rather than calculated because the trigger has not been established. Conditional deadlines have no date to sort by and are the ones most often lost - see the critical-date list.

description: Defendants to give Plaintiffs and the Court a minimum of 60 days advance notice before proceeding with foreclosure
triggering_event: Defendants electing to proceed with foreclosure
governing_rule: Doc. 34 at 26 ('should Defendants elect to proceed with foreclosure, Defendants shall provide Plaintiffs (and the Court) with a minimum of 60 days advance notice')
computation_method: NOT COMPUTED. This is a standing compliance obligation imposed on Defendants with no date of its own; it converts into a 60-day period only when Defendants elect to proceed. It binds until modified by the court.
consequence_of_missing: A foreclosure noticed on less than 60 days' advance notice to Plaintiffs and the Court would violate a standing order of the district judge. For Plaintiffs, missing the notice when it arrives forfeits the 60-day window to seek relief.
ambiguity_description: The order does not state the form the notice must take, whether the 60 days runs from the notice's date or its receipt, or whether notice to the Court means a filing on the docket.
verification_required: Monitor the docket for any notice of intent to foreclose. Confirm whether any such notice has been given since 2026-07-20.
notes: An obligation with no single date, and therefore easy to lose entirely. Recorded here so it is tracked. Doc. 34 at 4 records Defendants' stated plan to re-notice a sale if the matter is not resolved.

description: Clerk to submit the case to the magistrate judge
computation_method: No computation required. The order ties this to the expiration of the DL-001 deadline: 'The Clerk is DIRECTED to submit this case to the undersigned at the expiration of that deadline.'
consequence_of_missing: None as to the parties; this is an internal court action. Its practical effect is that the magistrate judge takes the case up on or about this date, which is why the state of the pleading on that date matters.
notes: Recorded because it tells the parties when the case lands back in front of the magistrate judge who cautioned about dismissal.

description: Default period for responding to an amended pleading
computation_method: NOT COMPUTED, and deliberately so. Rule 15(a)(3) supplies a default period, but Doc. 35 sets its own period running from filing. The specific order displaces the general rule. This row exists only to record that the two measure from different events, so that the conflict with DL-002 is visible rather than silently resolved.
consequence_of_missing: Recording this row prevents the default rule being applied by habit where an order says otherwise.
ambiguity_description: Rule 15(a)(3) and Doc. 35 use different triggering events (service vs. filing).
verification_required: Attorney to confirm that Doc. 35 controls over the Rule 15(a)(3) default, which is the ordinary result but should be verified against Eleventh Circuit and N.D. Ga. practice.
notes: Typed estimated, not calculated, because no input is established. Its date must read NOT-COMPUTABLE.

description: Rule 26(f) conference and Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures
triggering_event: Entry of a scheduling order or the start of the discovery period under the local rules
computation_method: NOT COMPUTED. No scheduling order is among the available sources, and the local-rule mechanics for the start of discovery in this district have not been obtained. Computing a discovery date from the national rules alone would ignore local rules that commonly displace them.
consequence_of_missing: Discovery served before the Rule 26(f) conference is premature under Rule 26(d)(1) and is subject to objection; discovery served late may be refused.
ambiguity_description: Whether any Rule 26(f) conference has occurred is unknown. SRC-004, dated 2026-08-19, refers to the Rule 26(f) conference in the future tense, which suggests it had not occurred by that date.
verification_required: Obtain the docket, any scheduling order, and N.D. Ga. Local Rules 16 and 26 before any discovery deadline is asserted.
notes: Flagged because SRC-004 (Plaintiffs' Rule 34 requests, dated 2026-08-19) may have been served before any Rule 26(f) conference. That is a legal question, routed to research as OLQ-4, not resolved here.
